title: Vacuum wound therapy
what: A special sponge is placed on the wound, covered with a film, and connected to a small pump. The pump gently draws off fluid and helps the wound heal.
why: For large wounds that are slow to heal, after operations, with a diabetic foot, and with pressure sores.
duration: a dressing change usually takes 20 to 40 minutes, every 2 to 3 days; treatment lasts from a few days to weeks
tell_doctor: Bleeding from the wound or clotting disorders
Pain during dressing changes. Ask for pain relief in advance

prepare.title: Pain relief
prepare.text: If dressing changes hurt, you can take a painkiller beforehand. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: The pump
prepare.text: If treatment is at home, learn how to check the pump and what to do when it alarms.

bring: The pump charger, if treatment is at home
steps: The old dressing is carefully removed
The wound is cleaned and examined
The sponge is cut to the shape of the wound and placed in it
Everything is covered with clear film
The tube and pump are connected
The seal is checked to make sure the dressing holds the vacuum
feel: When the pump starts, a pulling feeling in the wound
A dressing change can be unpleasant
The pump sometimes hums quietly or beeps
after: The pump should run all the time. Do not turn it off for long on your own
Watch the canister: if it is full, call the clinic
Come for dressing changes on schedule
red_flags: Blood in the tube or canister: turn off the pump and call your doctor or your local emergency number right away
The pump beeps and does not hold the vacuum
Fever, severe pain, bad smell from the wound

faq.q: Can I walk around with the pump?
faq.a: Usually yes. The pump is small and is carried on a strap or in a bag.
It depends on the wound. The doctor checks healing at every dressing change.

reminders.text: Vacuum dressing change tomorrow. Charge the pump and ask your doctor about pain relief in advance.
